content: 1. Sulbactam is actively secreted via OATP1, which constitutes a significant portion of its total clearance. Inhibition of OATP1 may lead to increased plasma concentrations of sulbactam. Close monitoring is recommended. 2. Co-administration of sulbactam/durlobactam with dostarlimab may reduce the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Co-administration of sulbactam/durlobactam with durvalumab may reduce the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Eluxadoline may increase the plasma levels or effects of sulbactam/durlobactam through an unspecified mechanism. Avoid or consider alternative drugs. 5. Enasidenib may increase the plasma levels or effects of sulbactam/durlobactam through an unspecified mechanism. Avoid or consider alternative drugs. Avoid co-administration of enasidenib with sensitive OATP1B1, OATP1B3, or BCRP substrates, as even minimal concentration changes may result in serious toxicities. If unavoidable, reduce the substrate dosage as per prescribing information. 6. Encorafenib may increase the plasma levels or effects of sulbactam/durlobactam through an unspecified mechanism. Co-administration of sulbactam/durlobactam with oral microbiota products may reduce their efficacy due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Oral microbiota products contain bacterial spores, and antibacterial agents may decrease their efficacy. Complete antibiotic regimens 2–4 days before initiating oral microbiota therapy. Monitor closely. 14. Co-administration of sulbactam/durlobactam with nivolumab may reduce the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Liver test abnormalities (19%), diarrhea (17%), anemia (13%), hypokalemia (12%), arrhythmia (9%), acute kidney injury (6%), thrombocytopenia (6%), and constipation (6%) are potential adverse effects. 32. Sulbactam and durlobactam are contraindicated in patients with a history of severe hypersensitivity to these agents or other beta-lactam antibacterial drugs. 33. There are no available data on the use of sulbactam plus durlobactam during pregnancy to evaluate the risk of major birth defects, miscarriage, or other adverse maternal or fetal outcomes. Published data on sulbactam in combination with ampicillin during pregnancy have not identified a drug-associated risk of major birth defects or adverse outcomes. No human data are available for durlobactam. 34. Sulbactam is present in human milk in low concentrations, but there are no data on the presence of durlobactam in human or animal milk. 35. Prepared solutions of sulbactam/durlobactam should be brought to ambient room temperature (15–30 minutes) before infusion. Administer all doses via IV infusion over 3 hours. Vials do not contain bacteriostatic preservatives. 36. The above information is provided for general informational and educational purposes only.
